questions.q: In a 5-stage instruction pipeline consisting of IF, ID, EX, MEM, and WB stages, which type of hazard occurs when an instruction depends on the result of a previous instruction that has not yet completed execution, and how is it most efficiently resolved in hardware without inserting pipeline stalls?
options: Data hazard; resolved via operand forwarding (data bypassing)
Structural hazard; resolved via branch prediction logic
Control hazard; resolved via delayed branching
Data hazard; resolved by increasing clock frequency

questions.q: A computer system features a 2-way set-associative cache with 64 KB total capacity and 64-byte cache line size. If the main memory uses 32-bit byte addresses, how many bits are used for the Tag, Set Index, and Block Offset fields respectively?
options: Tag = 18 bits, Set Index = 8 bits, Offset = 6 bits
Tag = 16 bits, Set Index = 10 bits, Offset = 6 bits
Tag = 17 bits, Set Index = 9 bits, Offset = 6 bits
Tag = 20 bits, Set Index = 6 bits, Offset = 6 bits

questions.q: According to Flynn's taxonomy of computer architectures, which class represents modern Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) and SIMD vector extensions where a single instruction operates concurrently across multiple data streams?
In interrupt-driven I/O processing, what is the primary technical distinction between a vectored interrupt and a non-vectored interrupt?
options: Vectored interrupts cannot be masked by software, whereas non-vectored interrupts are always maskable
Non-vectored interrupts use Direct Memory Access (DMA), while vectored interrupts require programmed I/O
Vectored interrupts are generated only by software exceptions, whereas non-vectored interrupts are strictly hardware-driven
In vectored interrupts, the interrupting device directly supplies the interrupt vector address to the CPU, whereas in non-vectored interrupts, the CPU branches to a fixed address and polls devices

questions.q: In IEEE 754 single-precision (32-bit) floating-point representation, what are the bit allocations for Sign, Biased Exponent, and Mantissa (Fraction), and what is the bias value used for the exponent?
options: Sign = 1 bit, Exponent = 11 bits, Mantissa = 20 bits, Bias = 1023
Sign = 1 bit, Exponent = 8 bits, Mantissa = 23 bits, Bias = 127
Sign = 1 bit, Exponent = 7 bits, Mantissa = 24 bits, Bias = 63
Sign = 2 bits, Exponent = 8 bits, Mantissa = 22 bits, Bias = 128

questions.q: In the context of deadlock avoidance, Dijkstra's Banker's Algorithm determines whether granting a resource request leaves the system in a 'safe state'. A state is considered safe if and only if:
options: The total number of available resource instances exceeds the total requested resources of all running processes combined
No process holds a shared resource while simultaneously requesting an exclusive lock
Every resource type has exactly one instance currently unassigned in physical memory
There exists at least one safe execution sequence of processes such that every process can satisfy its maximum resource claims

questions.q: Which CPU scheduling phenomenon occurs under First-Come-First-Served (FCFS) scheduling where multiple I/O-bound processes are forced to wait for long periods behind a single long CPU-burst process, resulting in poor CPU and device utilization?

In virtual memory management, Belady's Anomaly describes a counter-intuitive situation where increasing the number of page frames results in an increased number of page faults. Under which page replacement algorithm is Belady's Anomaly observed?
Consider a counting semaphore S initialized to the value 7. If 12 wait() (P) operations and 8 signal() (V) operations are executed on S, what will be the resulting value of S?
In a Unix/Linux ext4 file system, what information is NOT stored directly inside an inode data structure?
options: Direct and indirect disk block pointers

questions.q: A relation R(A, B, C, D) has the following functional dependencies: A -> B, B -> C, and C -> D. If the primary key of relation R is A, in which normal form does relation R currently reside?

In database transaction processing, which schedule property guarantees that if a transaction T_j reads a value written by T_i, then T_i must commit before T_j reads that value, thereby eliminating cascading rollbacks entirely?
In a B+ Tree index of order m (where m is the maximum number of pointers in an internal node), which of the following architectural properties is TRUE?
options: Internal nodes store data record pointers alongside keys to minimize tree height
Leaf nodes may appear at different depths depending on insertion order
A leaf node cannot have fewer than m keys under any circumstances
All data records or key-pointer pairs reside exclusively in the leaf nodes, which are linked together in a doubly linked list

questions.q: Under the ANSI SQL standard isolation levels, which transaction anomaly is prevented by REPEATABLE READ that is NOT prevented by READ COMMITTED?
In relational algebra, which fundamental operation produces a relation containing all tuples that are in relation R but NOT in relation S, provided R and S are union-compatible?
Using the Master Theorem, what is the asymptotic time complexity of the recurrence relation: T(n) = 4T(n/2) + O(n²) ?
In an AVL tree, after inserting an element into the left subtree of the right child of a node, which type of rotation sequence must be performed to restore the balance factor of the violated node?
Why is Bellman-Ford algorithm preferred over Dijkstra's algorithm for finding single-source shortest paths in certain weighted directed graphs?
options: Bellman-Ford operates in O(V log V + E) time, which is strictly faster than Dijkstra's algorithm
Bellman-Ford can correctly handle graphs with negative edge weights and detect negative-weight cycles, whereas Dijkstra's algorithm fails
Bellman-Ford works exclusively on Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) without using priority queues
Dijkstra requires memory proportional to O(V²), making it inapplicable to sparse networks

questions.q: What is the theoretical lower bound for the number of key comparisons required in the worst case to sort an array of n arbitrary elements using any comparison-based sorting algorithm?

In a hash table utilizing open addressing with linear probing, what is the primary structural drawback that causes consecutive occupied slots to form long contiguous blocks, thereby significantly degrading search performance?
What is the space complexity of the optimal Dynamic Programming tabular approach for finding the length of the Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) between two strings of lengths m and n?
options: O(2^(m+n)) exponential space in all implementations
O(m + n) strictly without possibility of reduction
O(m × n), which can be optimized to O(min(m, n)) if only the length is required

questions.q: During the TCP connection termination handshake, which state must the active closer transition into after sending the final ACK segment, and what is the standard duration it remains in that state before completely releasing socket resources?
options: TIME_WAIT state, lasting 2 × Maximum Segment Lifetime (2MSL)
CLOSE_WAIT state, lasting 1 × Maximum Segment Lifetime (1MSL)
FIN_WAIT_2 state, lasting indefinitely until keep-alive timer expires

questions.q: An enterprise organization is assigned the IPv4 network block 192.168.10.0/24. The network engineer needs to carve out subnets to support at least 28 usable host IP addresses per subnet. What subnet mask should be assigned, and how many valid subnets can be created?
options: 255.255.255.240 (/28), providing 16 subnets with 14 usable hosts each
255.255.255.192 (/26), providing 4 subnets with 62 usable hosts each
255.255.255.224 (/27), providing 8 subnets with 30 usable hosts each
255.255.255.248 (/29), providing 32 subnets with 6 usable hosts each

questions.q: In TCP congestion control (Tahoe and Reno), when a transmission timeout occurs (coarse timer expiry), how do the Slow Start Threshold (ssthresh) and Congestion Window (cwnd) adapt?
options: cwnd is halved and ssthresh remains unchanged (entering Fast Recovery)
cwnd is set to ssthresh and increases exponentially
ssthresh is set to max(FlightSize/2, 2*SMSS) and cwnd is reset to 1 SMSS (entering Slow Start)
ssthresh is doubled and cwnd is reduced to zero

questions.q: Which of the following routing protocols is classified as an Exterior Gateway Protocol (EGP) based on Path Vector mechanics, operating over TCP port 179 to exchange reachability information across Autonomous Systems (AS)?

What is the maximum sender window size in a Selective Repeat sliding window protocol if sequence numbers are represented using n bits, in order to avoid ambiguity between new frames and retransmitted duplicate frames?
What is the primary role of the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) in the TCP/IP network protocol stack?
options: To map a physical MAC address to an assigned logical IPv4 address upon system boot
To resolve a known logical IPv4 address to its corresponding physical MAC address on a local area network
To translate human-readable domain names into routable public IP addresses
To dynamically allocate private IP addresses to newly connected DHCP clients

questions.q: In Scrum Agile methodology, which ceremony is held at the conclusion of a sprint specifically for the team to inspect its internal processes, collaboration dynamics, and engineering practices in order to plan quality and process improvements?

In McCabe's Cyclomatic Complexity metric, given a control flow graph G with E edges, N nodes, and P connected components, what is the formula used to calculate the cyclomatic complexity V(G) to determine the number of independent basis paths?
In Basic COCOMO software cost estimation, which development mode corresponds to small software teams working in familiar, in-house environments with relaxed requirements and experienced developers?

Which Gang of Four (GoF) design pattern defines a one-to-many dependency between objects such that when one object changes its state, all its registered dependents are notified and updated automatically?
In Java Virtual Machine (JVM) memory architecture, where are class metadata, method bytecode, runtime constant pools, and static variables stored in Java 8 and subsequent versions?

In C++, how is the classic 'Diamond Problem' of multiple inheritance (where two derived classes inherit from a common base class, and a final class inherits from both derived classes) resolved to prevent duplicate base class instances?
options: By declaring all member functions of the base class as 'static'
By overloading the assignment operator in the most derived class
By declaring the common base class as 'virtual' during inheritance in the intermediate derived classes
By marking the most derived class with the 'final' specifier

questions.q: In Java, what happens during dynamic method dispatch (runtime polymorphism) when a superclass reference variable invokes an overridden method on a subclass instance?
options: The compiler binds the method call at compile time based strictly on the reference type
The JVM looks up the method implementation at runtime using the instance's virtual method table (vtable) and executes the subclass version
The JVM throws an IllegalAccessError unless explicitly cast to the subclass type
The superclass method executes first, followed automatically by the subclass method

questions.q: Since Java 8, interfaces can contain non-abstract method implementations. Which keyword must be used to declare an interface method with a default implementation that implementing classes may inherit or override?
In Java exception handling, what requirement must an object meet to be declared within the parentheses of a try-with-resources statement to guarantee automatic resource deallocation?
options: It must be declared with the 'transient' modifier
It must implement either java.lang.AutoCloseable or java.io.Closeable interface

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an architectural constraint of the Representational State Transfer (REST) architectural style as defined by Roy Fielding?
What is the semantic difference between HTTP status code 401 (Unauthorized) and HTTP status code 403 (Forbidden)?
options: 401 indicates authentication credentials are required or have failed verification, whereas 403 indicates the client is authenticated but lacks required permissions for the resource
401 applies exclusively to HTTPS connections, whereas 403 applies exclusively to plain HTTP
401 indicates a server-side runtime error, whereas 403 indicates a client-side invalid payload format
401 indicates temporary rate limiting, whereas 403 indicates the resource has been permanently moved

questions.q: A JSON Web Token (JWT) comprises three Base64URL-encoded segments separated by periods. What are these three segments in sequence?

During Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS), when a web client makes a non-simple cross-origin HTTP request (e.g., using PUT or custom headers), what preflight HTTP request method is automatically dispatched by the browser before the actual request?
In modern symmetric cryptography, Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) operates on fixed 128-bit blocks using key lengths of:
options: 128, 192, or 256 bits with 10, 12, or 14 transformation rounds respectively
64, 128, or 256 bits with 8, 10, or 12 transformation rounds respectively
128, 256, or 512 bits with 16, 20, or 24 transformation rounds respectively

questions.q: In public-key cryptography and digital signatures, what ensures both the integrity of the transmitted message and the non-repudiation of the sender?
options: The sender encrypts the entire plaintext message using the recipient's public key
The recipient computes a checksum and transmits their shared symmetric key back to the sender
The sender prepends an unencrypted timestamp and salt to the ciphertext
The sender encrypts the cryptographic hash of the message using their private key

questions.q: Which web application attack involves an attacker tricking an authenticated victim's web browser into executing an unauthorized action on a trusted web application where the victim is currently authenticated, commonly mitigated by Anti-CSRF Synchronizer Tokens?
What mathematical property must a cryptographic hash function satisfy to ensure that it is computationally infeasible to find ANY two distinct input messages m1 and m2 such that Hash(m1) = Hash(m2)?
Which foundational security tenet defines the 'Zero Trust' security architecture framework mandated in modern banking infrastructure?
options: Implicit trust is granted to all traffic originating within the corporate intranet perimeter
'Never Trust, Always Verify' across all users, devices, applications, and data packets regardless of network location
Security verification is enforced only during initial login and disabled for active sessions
Air-gapped physical servers are exempt from periodic credential rotation

questions.q: In cloud computing, what is the core difference between a Type-1 (Bare Metal) Hypervisor and a Type-2 (Hosted) Hypervisor?
options: Type-1 hypervisors support only containerized workloads, whereas Type-2 hypervisors support full hardware virtualization
Type-1 hypervisors cannot manage multicore processors, whereas Type-2 hypervisors support unlimited CPU cores
Type-1 hypervisors run directly on the physical hardware without an underlying host OS, whereas Type-2 hypervisors execute on top of an existing host OS
Type-2 hypervisors offer significantly lower virtualization latency than Type-1 hypervisors

questions.q: Under the Cloud Shared Responsibility Model for Platform as a Service (PaaS), which layer is typically managed by the cloud service provider rather than the enterprise customer?
options: Operating System patching, middleware runtime, and server hardware infrastructure
Application code, custom business logic, and database user schema
Customer data access control and role-based permissions
Client endpoint device configuration and local network firewall

questions.q: Which Linux kernel features provide resource isolation (CPU, memory, network, process tree) that enable lightweight containerization engines such as Docker to operate without full guest OS hypervisors?
options: SELinux policy modules and AppArmor profiles only
Virtual Network Interface Cards and eBPF filters

questions.q: Which cloud storage type stores data as distinct objects containing data payload, unique identifier, and customizable metadata, accessed over standard REST APIs (e.g., HTTP GET/PUT), making it ideal for unstructured big data?
In supervised machine learning, how does high model variance typically manifest, and what is the standard mathematical mitigation?
options: Underfitting with high bias on training data; mitigated by simplifying the model architecture
Overfitting on training data with poor test generalization; mitigated by regularization (L1/L2), cross-validation, and pruning
Inability to converge during gradient descent; mitigated by increasing the learning rate
Complete saturation of weights; mitigated by removing hidden layers

questions.q: Why is the Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) activation function f(x) = max(0, x) widely preferred over the Sigmoid function in hidden layers of deep neural networks?
options: It strictly constrains output values to a symmetric range between -1 and +1
It is continuously differentiable across all real numbers including zero
It prevents dead neurons under all negative input conditions automatically
It mitigates the vanishing gradient problem for positive inputs and requires significantly less computational overhead

questions.q: In Apache Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS), what is the primary role of the NameNode?
options: To physically store and serve file data blocks and handle disk I/O requests directly from clients
To maintain the filesystem directory tree and metadata mapping of data blocks to physical DataNodes in memory
To execute Map and Reduce computation tasks on cluster worker nodes
To replace failed disk drives automatically using hardware RAID controller logic

questions.q: In blockchain distributed ledger technology, which vulnerability allows an entity or mining cartel controlling more than 50% of the network hash rate to rewrite transaction history and perform double-spending attacks?
Which lightweight, publish-subscribe network protocol designed for constrained IoT devices and low-bandwidth networks runs over TCP and utilizes a central broker to manage message topics?

In India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) ecosystem managed by NPCI, what technical entity functions as the central transaction routing switch, connecting PSP bank applications to issuing Core Banking Systems (CBS)?
options: Immediate Payment Service (IMPS) ATM Switch only
National Financial Switch (NFS) / Unified Payments Interface Switch
Clearing Corporation of India Limited (CCIL) Settlement Terminal

questions.q: What is the key settlement difference between the National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) system and the Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system operating under Reserve Bank of India oversight?
options: NEFT operates strictly for transactions exceeding Rs. 2 Lakhs, whereas RTGS has no minimum limit
NEFT is available only during banking branch hours, whereas RTGS operates 24x7x365
NEFT settles fund transfers in half-hourly batches on a net settlement basis, whereas RTGS processes and settles each transaction continuously on an individual gross basis
RTGS transactions can be revoked within 15 minutes of initiation, whereas NEFT is irrevocable

questions.q: In global and domestic financial interbank electronic messaging, which standard provides a rich, XML/JSON-based data dictionary to replace legacy ISO 8583 and MT format telegraphic financial messages?
Under the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Cyber Security Framework for Banks, what is the mandatory requirement regarding the reporting of critical cybersecurity incidents to the regulator?
options: Incidents must be compiled and submitted solely in the quarterly audit review
Incident notification is voluntary for non-scheduled cooperative banks
Reporting is required only if monetary financial loss exceeds Rs. 10 Crores
Banks must report all critical cybersecurity incidents to the RBI / CERT-In within 2 to 6 hours of detection

questions.q: According to the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS), which of the following sensitive authentication data (SAD) must NEVER be stored by an acquiring merchant or payment gateway post-authorization under any circumstances, even if encrypted?
options: Full magnetic stripe data (track 2) or Card Verification Value (CVV/CVC)

questions.q: Which normal form removes transitive functional dependencies of non-key attributes?
questions.explanation: Third normal form requires that every non-key attribute depend only on a candidate key, not transitively on it.

questions.q: What does a database write-ahead log guarantee?
questions.explanation: Write-ahead logging records undo/redo information before the corresponding data pages are overwritten.
options: Data changes are written before the log
Log records are written before corresponding dirty pages are persisted
Indexes are never written to disk

questions.q: Consider P = 3 processes and R = 2 resource types with 5 instances in a system. In Banker's Algorithm, a state is safe if:
questions.explanation: Safety requires existence of a complete process execution sequence, with resources released after completion.
options: There is one process for which Available equals zero
Every process can finish in some sequence using Available and its future releases
Every process holds at least one resource

questions.q: Which TCP mechanism primarily limits the amount of unacknowledged data sent by a sender?
questions.explanation: The TCP receive window is used for end-to-end flow control.

questions.q: In asymmetric cryptography, a message encrypted with a party's public key can be decrypted only by:
questions.explanation: Public-key encryption uses a recipient's public key and requires the matching private key for decryption.
options: Any holder of the public key
The party holding the matching private key
The CA that issued the certificate
The recipient's symmetric session key only

questions.q: Which banking technology controls the real-time transfer of interbank payment instructions and is associated with immediate settlement in some systems?
questions.explanation: RTGS processes and settles qualifying interbank transfers individually and in real time, subject to cutoff and operational rules.

questions.q: Which OAuth 2.0 grant is generally appropriate for a server-side confidential application acting on its own behalf?
questions.explanation: The client credentials grant authenticates a confidential client for machine-to-machine access.

questions.q: In Docker, which isolation unit is a running instance of an image?
questions.explanation: A container is a runnable isolated instance created from an image.

questions.q: Which test type verifies that a change does not break existing behavior?
questions.explanation: Regression testing checks that software changes have not adversely affected existing functionality.

questions.q: Which Linux command performs a live search over process information and supports interactive management?
questions.explanation: top provides a live, periodically refreshed view of system processes and resource usage.
